$comment: The crosswalk as reviewers who teach to this curriculum wrote it, point by point, from the official text (scripts/curricula/apply-review.js --authored). `why` is the reviewer's reason; the registry's builder adds each row's grade and writes crosswalk.json.

K:position-words.why: Position words are the 'geometrisk sprog i hverdagssituationer' the børnehaveklasse goal names; they come before 'anvende geometriske begreber' efter 3. klassetrin.

K:scene-search.why: Only the shape sheets fit: finding the shape of everyday objects is 'geometrisk sprog i hverdagssituationer'; the plain picture search is visual attention and has no goal.

K:compare-size-extremes.why: Biggest / tallest / longest is the comparing language of 'geometrisk sprog i hverdagssituationer'; direct comparison comes before 'måle' in MAT.3.K3.

K:order-by-size.why: Ordering by size or height uses the size language of the goal 'geometrisk sprog i hverdagssituationer' and is a step before measuring (MAT.3.K3 'måle').

K:patterns.why: Patterns by shape, size and position are standard content of 'Matematisk opmærksomhed' and are described with 'geometrisk sprog'; no goal efter 3. klassetrin names patterns, so no second row.

K:one-to-one.why: Pairing one to one uses no number yet; it is the step before 'antalsbestemmelse' in the point of attention and before 'anvende tal'.

K:compare-groups.why: More / fewer / equal is 'anvende tal ... i hverdagssituationer'; done without numerals it only prepares 'ordne talsymbolerne'.

K:count-how-many.why: Counting a set and writing or matching the numeral is exactly 'genkende ... talsymbolerne og anvende dem til antalsbestemmelse'; to 10-20 it is a smaller range than 'trecifrede tal til at beskrive antal'.

K:subitize.why: Seeing a small quantity at a glance is using number ('anvende tal'); it supports 'antalsbestemmelse' but the sheets need no numeral.

K:conservation.why: That the number stays the same however the things lie is part of using number in børnehaveklassen; it underlies 'antalsbestemmelse'.

K:count-out-n.why: The child reads a numeral and makes that many: 'genkende ... talsymbolerne og anvende dem til antalsbestemmelse'.

K:shape-naming.why: Naming circle, triangle, square is 'geometrisk sprog'; it prepares 'anvende geometriske begreber' efter 3. klassetrin.

K:numeral-formation.why: The point of attention asks the child to 'genkende ... talsymbolerne'; tracing and writing 0-20 practises the symbols (writing itself is not named, recognition is).

K:colour-by-number.why: Following a numeral key is recognising the number symbols: 'genkende ... talsymbolerne'.

K:classify-count-kinds.why: Counting each kind is 'antalsbestemmelse' in an everyday scene; sort-then-count is the first step toward 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

K:count-sides.why: Counting the sides of a shape joins both halves of the goal: 'tal og geometrisk sprog'.

K:count-forward-missing.why: Filling a count strip is 'genkende og ordne talsymbolerne'; to 20 it prepares 'beskrive ... rækkefølge' with larger numbers.

K:dot-to-dot-sequence.why: Joining numbered dots in order is 'ordne talsymbolerne' (the 11-30 sheets go a little beyond what most børnehaveklasser reach).

K:one-more-one-less.why: Count, add one, name the new number: number order used for 'antalsbestemmelse'; it is the idea before calculation methods in MAT.3.K2.

K:before-after-back.why: Before / after / between and counting back is 'ordne talsymbolerne'.

K:ordinal-position.why: Finding the 3rd in a line is using number for order in an everyday situation; MAT.3.O1 names 'rækkefølge' but with three-digit numbers.

K:days-of-week.why: The børnehaveklasse wording names only number and geometric language; the weekdays are a first step toward 'tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

K:tally-marks.why: Reading a tally back as a number is 'antalsbestemmelse' with number symbols; tallying is the recording step of 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

K:estimate.why: Guessing a quantity and checking by counting is using number and 'antalsbestemmelse'.

K:heavy-light.why: The børnehaveklasse goal names 'tal og geometrisk sprog', not weight; comparing heavier and lighter is the step before 'anslå og måle ... vægt'.

K:draw-shapes.why: Drawing named shapes with their sides and corners uses 'geometrisk sprog'.

K:combine-groups.why: Putting two groups together and counting all is 'anvende tal'; it is the idea of addition before the methods of MAT.3.K2.

K:take-away.why: Crossing out and counting what is left is 'anvende tal'; it is the idea of subtraction before the methods of MAT.3.K2.

K:count-on.why: Counting on from a known group is using number at børnehaveklasse level and the first calculation strategy toward 'metoder til beregninger'.

K:number-bonds-k.why: Splitting numbers to 10 into two parts (talvenner) is using number; in Danish schools the systematic work sits in 1. klasse, where it founds 'metoder til beregninger'.

K:compose-shapes.why: Building figures from tangram pieces uses shape language ('geometrisk sprog').

K:mirror-image.why: Recognising a mirror image needs no number or shape word, so the børnehaveklasse wording does not cover it; it prepares the concept of spejling under 'geometriske begreber'.

K:odd-even-pairing.why: Pairing up and seeing one left over is using number with objects; lige og ulige tal as a number property belongs to 1.-2. klasse.

K:teen-numbers.why: Reading 11-19 and using them for a quantity is 'talsymbolerne ... til antalsbestemmelse'; seeing them as ten and some more is the first step of place value toward 'trecifrede tal'.

K:fact-fluency-colour-code.why: Fluent adding and subtracting goes beyond 'anvende tal ... i hverdagssituationer'; it is the content of 'addere og subtrahere enkle naturlige tal med hovedregning', which Danish schools place in 1. klasse.

K:number-bonds-20.why: Number bonds to 20 are beyond the børnehaveklasse goal; they are a 1. klasse basis for 'metoder til beregninger med naturlige tal'.

1:add-within-10-models.why: Adding with a picture, ten-frame or dice model is 'udvikle metoder til beregninger'; it comes before 'hovedregning'.

1:subtract-cross-out.why: Subtracting by crossing out a picture model is an early method ('udvikle metoder til beregninger') before 'hovedregning'.

1:write-the-equation.why: Writing the whole number sentence for a picture belongs to 'Tal og algebra': the written form of the calculation.

1:patterns-missing.why: No goal names patterns; finding the rule of a pattern and filling the gaps is mathematical reasoning, the nearest wording is 'handle hensigtsmæssigt i situationer med matematik'.

1:sort-three-groups.why: Sorting into groups is the step before counting and showing data in 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

1:make-10.why: Tiervenner are the basis of the calculation methods of 1. klasse and of 'hovedregning'.

1:shape-attributes.why: Naming shapes by their defining properties is 'anvende geometriske begreber'.

1:ordinal-numbers.why: Ordinal numbers describe 'rækkefølge', but with small numbers, not the 'trecifrede tal' the point names.

1:number-line-placement.why: Placing numbers to 50 on a number line is 'beskrive ... rækkefølge' in a smaller range than 'trecifrede tal'.

1:count-on-back-hops.why: Hops on a number line are a method in the sense of 'udvikle metoder til beregninger'; with the drawn line it is not yet 'hovedregning'.

1:word-problems.why: A word problem is a 'situation med matematik' the pupil must act sensibly in, solved with addition and subtraction of natural numbers.

1:picture-graphs-sort-count.why: Sorting into a table, reading a picture graph and finding the most is 'udføre enkle statistiske undersøgelser' at 1. klasse level.

1:doubles-halves.why: Doubling and halving to 20 are calculation methods ('metoder til beregninger med naturlige tal').

1:odd-even-pairs.why: Lige og ulige tal by sharing between two belongs to 'Tal og algebra'; the fair sharing is an early halving method. The wording does not name odd and even.

1:near-doubles.why: Solving 6 + 7 as a double plus one is a mental strategy: 'udvikle metoder' and 'addere ... med hovedregning'.

1:add-three-addends.why: Adding three numbers is calculation with natural numbers at 1. klasse level.

1:fact-families.why: Using that addition and subtraction undo each other is a method for calculating ('udvikle metoder til beregninger').

1:missing-number-equations.why: Finding the unknown in a number sentence is early algebra under 'Tal og algebra', solved by calculation within 20.

1:true-false-equations.why: The meaning of the equal sign belongs to 'Tal og algebra'; the child calculates both sides. The goal's wording itself only names calculation.

1:bar-model.why: A part-part-whole bar is a drawn method for addition and subtraction ('udvikle metoder til beregninger').

1:tangram-compose.why: Composing figures from shapes is 'anvende geometriske begreber'.

1:days-months-seasons.why: Days and months are calendar knowledge before 'anslå og måle ... tid'; the seasons part is 'genkende natur ... i sin hverdag'.

1:days-months-seasons~season-wheel.why: The season wheel is 'genkende natur ... i sin hverdag' (årstiderne); the months in order prepare 'tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

1:measure-length-units.why: Measuring with unit cubes is 'måle' at 1. klasse level; it comes before measuring length in standard units as the point of attention expects.

1:time-read.why: Reading the clock to the hour and half hour is 'måle ... tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

1:fluency-within-20.why: Mental addition and subtraction within 20 is 'addere og subtrahere enkle naturlige tal med hovedregning'.

1:number-walls.why: Number walls (talmure) practise addition and finding a missing part by subtraction: calculation with natural numbers.

1:check-answers.why: Checking and correcting worked sums is calculation plus judging a result, which is to 'handle hensigtsmæssigt i situationer med matematik'.

1:bar-graphs.why: Reading and colouring a bar graph from counts is part of 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

1:tens-and-ones.why: Tens and ones is place value with two-digit numbers, the range below 'trecifrede tal', and the ground the calculation methods stand on.

1:number-words.why: Number names to 100 belong to knowing the numbers before 'trecifrede tal'. Danish number words (halvtreds, tres ...) are hard and deserve their own care.

1:compare-order-two-digit.why: Comparing and ordering is 'beskrive antal og rækkefølge', here with two-digit numbers, not yet three-digit.

1:hundreds-chart.why: The hundred chart shows the order of the numbers to 100: the range below 'trecifrede tal'.

1:one-ten-more-less.why: 1 and 10 more or less is a first calculation method with place value; the number range is below 'trecifrede tal'.

1:number-of-the-day.why: Showing one two-digit number in many ways is 'anvende ... tal til at beskrive antal' in a smaller range.

1:skip-counting.why: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s with equal groups is a calculation method (a running total) and number order within 100.

1:time-set-hands.why: Setting the clock hands is 'måle ... tid'; quarter hours and five minutes are usually 2. klasse in Denmark.

1:coins.why: Counting coins in a purse is a 'situation med matematik' from everyday life, solved by adding natural numbers (in Danish kroner: no cents).

1:open-number-line.why: The empty number line, where the child draws the jumps, is exactly 'udvikle metoder til beregninger'; it leads to 'hovedregning'.

1:mental-math-to-100.why: 34 + 20 and 56 - 4 in the head is 'addere og subtrahere enkle naturlige tal med hovedregning'; most Danish classes do this in 2. klasse.

1:bonds-to-100.why: Finding the partner to 100 is mental calculation with simple natural numbers.

2:bundle-ten-ones.why: Bundling ten ones is place value with two-digit numbers, the step before 'trecifrede tal' and before written calculation methods.

2:hundreds-chart-moves.why: Moves of +1 and +10 on the chart are a calculation method; the numbers stay under 100.

2:odd-even.why: Lige og ulige tal as two equal addends and by the ones digit belongs to 'Tal og algebra' (the wording itself only names calculation).

2:number-line-not-from-zero.why: Placing two-digit numbers on a cut number line is number order below the 'trecifrede tal' of the point.

2:2d-attributes.why: Sorting shapes by number of sides is 'anvende geometriske begreber'.

2:add-sub-within-100-practice.why: Adding and subtracting within 100 in number walls and mazes is calculation with natural numbers, mostly in the head.

2:two-step-word-problems.why: One- and two-step problems are 'situationer med matematik' to act sensibly in, solved by calculation within 100.

2:measure-with-ruler.why: Measuring with a ruler from 0 is 'måle længde' (in centimetres in Denmark).

2:compare-lengths.why: Measuring two objects and finding the difference is 'måle længde i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

2:read-build-3-digit.why: Reading and building three-digit numbers is the content of 'anvende trecifrede tal til at beskrive antal'.

2:expanded-form-digit-value.why: The value of each digit in a three-digit number is what 'anvende trecifrede tal' requires.

2:chart-within-1000.why: Counting on a chart 301-400 is 'trecifrede tal til at beskrive ... rækkefølge'.

2:skip-count-5-10-100.why: Counting in 5s, 10s and 100s is a calculation method and, by hundreds, order among three-digit numbers.

2:compare-order-3-digit.why: Comparing and ordering three-digit numbers is 'trecifrede tal til at beskrive antal og rækkefølge'.

2:hundred-more-less.why: 100 more and 100 less uses the hundreds place of three-digit numbers and is a mental calculation method.

2:time-5-min-quarter.why: Reading the clock to five minutes and the quarter hour is 'måle ... tid'.

2:calendar.why: Finding the weekday of a date and the days between two dates is 'måle ... tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

2:flat-or-solid.why: Telling plane figures from solids is 'anvende geometriske begreber'.

2:solids-in-real-life.why: Matching kugle, terning, cylinder, kegle, kasse and pyramide to real things is using geometric concepts.

2:3d-faces-edges-vertices.why: Counting flader, kanter and hjørner is 'anvende geometriske begreber' on solids.

2:add-with-blocks.why: Adding with base-ten blocks is a concrete calculation method with three-digit numbers.

2:subtract-with-blocks.why: Taking away base-ten blocks is a concrete calculation method with three-digit numbers.

2:column-method.why: The column method is one method for 'beregninger med naturlige tal'; note the goal says 'udvikle metoder', so Danish teaching starts from the pupils' own methods and often meets the standard algorithm in 3. klasse.

2:shopping-money.why: Prices, enough money and change are everyday 'situationer med matematik', solved by adding and subtracting.

2:bar-graphs.why: Making a bar graph from a tally and answering questions about it is 'udføre enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

2:line-plots.why: Reading a diagram of marks above numbers (prikdiagram) is reading data in a simple statistical investigation.

2:round-to-ten.why: Rounding to the nearest ten is a tool for estimating calculations (overslag) under 'Tal og algebra'; in Denmark it is more often met in 3. klasse.

2:mass-grams.why: Reading grams on a balance or scale is 'måle ... vægt'.

2:read-jugs.why: Reading a measuring jug is 'måle'; the point of attention names only 'længde, tid og vægt', so volume sits under the goal alone.

2:choose-units.why: Choosing a fitting unit is part of 'anslå og måle'. The Danish sheets must use cm/m, g/kg, ml/l only (no inches or feet).

2:equal-groups-times.why: From equal groups to repeated addition to the multiplication sentence is 'udvikle metoder til beregninger med naturlige tal'.

2:arrays.why: Rows and columns as a model for multiplication is a calculation method with natural numbers.

2:skip-count-3-4.why: Counting in 3s and 4s builds the tables: a method for calculating.

2:scaled-pictograph.why: Reading and making a pictograph where a picture stands for 2 is part of 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

2:share-and-group.why: Sharing equally and making equal groups is the start of division: 'metoder til beregninger med naturlige tal'.

2:equal-shares-shapes.why: Cutting shapes into equal parts uses geometric concepts; naming the parts as fractions goes beyond 'beregninger med naturlige tal' (brøker belong to the goals efter 6. klassetrin, not in this list).

2:fraction-of-a-set.why: The sharing itself is division with natural numbers, but the fraction notation 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 is beyond 'naturlige tal'.

2:symmetry-line.why: Deciding whether a line is a mirror line is 'anvende geometriske begreber' (spejlingsakse).

2:symmetry-complete.why: Completing a symmetrical grid picture is using the concept of spejling.

2:grid-coordinates.why: Finding a square by its code B2 is describing position in a grid, a geometric concept of indskolingen.

2:tangram-orientation.why: Telling a turned or flipped figure from the same one uses the concepts of drejning and spejling.

3:compare-4-digit.why: The point names 'trecifrede tal'; four-digit numbers go one place further on the same line.

3:rounding.why: Rounding to 10 and 100 serves estimating calculations with natural numbers ('Tal og algebra').

3:column-regrouping.why: Written addition and subtraction within 1000 is a method for 'beregninger med naturlige tal' at 3. klasse level.

3:estimate-by-rounding.why: Overslag is a calculation method, and judging whether an answer is reasonable is to 'handle hensigtsmæssigt i situationer med matematik'.

3:magic-squares.why: A magic square is addition and finding missing addends with natural numbers.

3:parity-of-sums.why: Reasoning about odd and even sums belongs to 'Tal og algebra'; the wording itself names only calculation.

3:arithmetic-patterns.why: Finding the constant step of a number pattern and continuing it is counting in steps: calculation with natural numbers under 'Tal og algebra'.

3:time-to-minute.why: Reading the analog clock to the minute is 'måle ... tid'.

3:mult-equal-groups.why: Reading a product as equal groups or an array is a method for multiplication with natural numbers.

3:mult-number-line.why: Equal jumps on a number line are a method for multiplication.

3:commutative.why: That a x b equals b x a is a property pupils use when they 'udvikle metoder til beregninger'.

3:times-tables.why: The tables, with unknown facts derived from known ones, are 'metoder til beregninger med naturlige tal'; the point of attention names only addition and subtraction.

3:scaled-graphs.why: Reading and building scaled bar graphs and pictographs is 'udføre enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

3:thermometer.why: Reading a scale is 'måle'; temperature is not among 'længde, tid og vægt' of the point of attention.

3:division-sharing.why: Division by equal sharing is a method for calculating with natural numbers.

3:division-repeated-subtraction.why: Division as equal hops back is a method for calculating with natural numbers.

3:mult-div-relationship.why: Using the tables for division and for an unknown factor is 'udvikle metoder til beregninger'.

3:muldiv-word-problems.why: Modelling a story as groups or group size is acting sensibly in a 'situation med matematik', then calculating.

3:input-output.why: A number machine (regnemaskine) asks for the rule and its inverse: early algebra under 'Tal og algebra', done by calculating.

3:balance-equations.why: Equations with an operation on both sides are early algebra under 'Tal og algebra'; the child calculates both sides.

3:add-subtract-time.why: Adding minutes and hours to a clock time is working with 'tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge'.

3:elapsed-duration.why: Finding how much time passed is 'måle ... tid'.

3:time-12-24.why: Denmark writes digital time on the 24-hour clock, so moving between 'klokken 3 om eftermiddagen' and 15.00 is 'tid i enkle hverdagssammenhænge' (there is no a.m./p.m. in Danish).

3:area-model.why: Area by counting squares is 'måle', and rows x columns is a multiplication method.

3:same-area.why: Rectangles with the same area and another shape: the concept of areal under 'Geometri og måling'.

3:perimeter.why: Omkreds as the distance around a shape is a geometric concept that is measured as a length.

3:same-perimeter.why: Telling omkreds from areal is 'anvende geometriske begreber og måle'.

3:division-remainder.why: Division with a remainder is calculation with natural numbers; many Danish classes meet it first in 4. klasse.

3:right-angles.why: Ret vinkel, and smaller or bigger than it, is a geometric concept.

3:classify-quadrilaterals.why: Sorting firkanter by their properties is 'anvende geometriske begreber'; the rhombus and the class inclusion (a square is a rectangle) are at the top of what indskolingen does.

3:symmetry.why: Finding and counting symmetriakser is using a geometric concept.

3:partition-equal-areas.why: Dividing a shape into equal areas uses geometric concepts; naming each part as a unit fraction goes beyond 'naturlige tal'.

3:fraction-unit-build.why: Fractions a/b are not 'naturlige tal'; brøker belong to the goals efter 6. klassetrin, which this list does not hold.

3:whole-from-unit.why: Rebuilding the whole from a unit fraction is fraction work beyond 'beregninger med naturlige tal'.

3:fraction-number-line.why: Fractions on the number line between 0 and 1 go beyond the natural numbers the goal names.

3:compare-fractions.why: Comparing fractions goes beyond the natural numbers the goal names.

3:equivalent-fractions.why: Equivalent fractions go beyond the natural numbers the goal names; in Denmark this is 4.-5. klasse content.

3:fraction-of-set.why: 1/3 of 12 is solved by dividing natural numbers, but the fraction notation is beyond 'naturlige tal'.

3:line-plot-halves.why: The child measures lengths ('måle') and shows the data in a diagram ('enkle statistiske undersøgelser'); half units are at the top of the level.

3:volume-cubes.why: Counting unit cubes in a solid, hidden ones too, is measuring rumfang and using spatial concepts.

K:pre-writing-strokes.why: Lines, loops and zigzags come before 'bogstavernes form' and before expressing oneself 'i skrift'.

K:all-about-me-personal.why: A self-portrait and 'my favourite things' is 'udtrykke sig i billeder'; it prepares expressing oneself 'i skrift ... og billede i nære og velkendte situationer'.

K:rhyme.why: Hearing rhyme is attention to the sound side of language (the 'Sprog' goal); it prepares the letter-sound knowledge of the point of attention.

K:category-sort.why: Sorting pictures under category words is vocabulary and concept work in the 'Sprog' area; the goal's wording is broad and does not name vocabulary.

K:letter-identification.why: Finding a letter among look-alikes is 'genkende alle bogstavernes form'. Note the point excludes q (and w, x, z), so b/d/p should carry the Danish sheets.

K:letter-formation.why: Tracing capitals and small letters fixes 'bogstavernes form'. The Danish alphabet has 29 letters: æ, ø, å must be in the set.

K:count-syllables.why: Clapping stavelser is language attention in børnehaveklassen; it prepares reading 'ord på to stavelser'.

K:letter-case.why: Matching capital and small letters is 'genkende alle bogstavernes form'.

K:beginning-sounds.why: Forlyd linked to a letter is 'bogstavernes ... lyd'.

K:category-odd-one-out.why: Saying which one does not belong uses category words: vocabulary work in the 'Sprog' area (the wording does not name it).

K:opposites.why: Modsætninger are word-meaning work in the 'Sprog' area (the wording is broad and does not name it).

K:alphabet-order.why: The point asks for the letters' 'form, navn og lyd'; their order goes one step further on the same line. In Danish the alphabet ends with æ, ø, å.

K:story-sequencing.why: Ordering story pictures is working with narrative, one of the 'måder at anvende sprog på'; it prepares understanding 'enkle tekster'.

K:sound-position.why: Hearing where a sound sits and naming the middle vowel uses 'bogstavernes ... lyd'; it prepares spelling 'lydrette' words.

K:vowels-consonants.why: Sorting letters into vokaler and konsonanter goes beyond 'form, navn og lyd'. Danish has nine vowels: a, e, i, o, u, y, æ, ø, å.

K:bilingual-cards.why: Seeing one word in two languages is being 'opmærksom på forskellige måder at anvende sprog på'.

K:segment-phonemes.why: Splitting a word into its sounds is language attention; it is the step before reading and spelling 'lydrette' words.

K:cvc-build.why: Building words like 'bil' and 'bus' goes beyond single letters' sound and is the start of 'stave til lydrette' words (fx 'ti, bil').

K:word-picture-match.why: Meeting written words for pictures is attention to written language; it prepares 'læse lydrette' words.

K:singular-plural.why: Ental og flertal is attention to how a word changes form: language attention in the 'Sprog' area.

K:digraphs-k.why: The point names single letters' sound. sh/ch/th are English; a Danish version can only use the few Danish letter teams at the start of a word (sj- in 'sjov', ch- in loan words), which goes beyond the point.

K:sight-words-reading.why: Reading frequent words (og, jeg, er, det) at sight is a first step toward 'almindelige ikke-lydrette ord' and 'læse enkle tekster'; børnehaveklassen has no reading goal.

K:word-sentence-tracing.why: Tracing words practises 'bogstavernes form'; writing left to right with spaces prepares 'udtrykke sig i skrift'.

K:articles.why: Choosing en or et for a noun is attention to the form of the language ('Sprog'); the wording does not name grammar.

1:rhyming.why: Rhyme is sound awareness, a step before reading and spelling 'lydrette' words; no goal efter 2. klassetrin names it.

1:phoneme-boxes.why: Sound by sound is how 'lydrette' words are spelled (segmenting) and read (blending).

1:digraphs.why: Only if rebuilt for Danish: sh/ch/th do not exist, but two letters for one sound (ng, sj, hv, hj, nd, ld) make the 'almindelige ikke-lydrette ord' the points name.

1:spell-picture-words.why: Writing the word for a picture is 'stave til lydrette ... ord' (fx 'ti, bil og kano').

1:syllables-split.why: Splitting and joining stavelser is how pupils read 'ord på to stavelser'.

1:syllable-vowel.why: 'Every syllable has a vowel' is a rule that supports reading and spelling two-syllable words; it is not itself what the points ask.

1:word-families-syllable-reading.why: Reading two-syllable words by their syllables is 'læse lydrette ... ord på to stavelser'; word reading prepares 'enkle tekster'.

1:alphabetical-order.why: No goal names alphabetical order; it builds on the letter knowledge of BH.0.O1 and goes beyond it. Danish order ends ... x, y, z, æ, ø, å.

1:opposites.why: Word-meaning work supports reading 'enkle tekster' and 'opmærksomhed på sprog'; no binding goal names vocabulary.

1:articles.why: Sorting nouns by en / et (fælleskøn, intetkøn) is attention to language; the goal itself is about communicating.

1:read-and-follow.why: Reading an instruction and doing what it says is to 'læse enkle tekster sikkert og bruge dem'.

1:cloze.why: Choosing the word that fits a sentence shows the child reads simple text with understanding.

1:synonyms.why: Words that mean the same are vocabulary work that supports reading and 'opmærksomhed på sprog'; no goal names it.

1:unscramble-sentence.why: Building one given sentence with capital letter and full stop is the step before one's own 'sammenhængende tekster på mindst 3 linjer'.

1:question-words.why: Reading hvem / hvad / hvor questions and matching answers is reading simple text with understanding; asking questions prepares communication.

1:story-sequencing.why: Ordering sentences to pictures is reading 'enkle tekster'; story structure prepares the talk about literature in 'Fortolkning'.

1:word-classes.why: Navneord, udsagnsord and tillægsord give 'opmærksomhed på sprog', but the goal is about communicating; the binding text no longer names ordklasser.

1:pronouns.why: Replacing a name with han / hun / de is attention to language; no goal names stedord.

1:shades-of-meaning.why: Ordering words from weak to strong is word-meaning work; it supports 'opmærksomhed på sprog' and reading.

1:root-words.why: Seeing the root in a longer word helps reading and spelling 'ikke-lydrette' words; morphemes are usually 2.-3. klasse work.

1:story-writing.why: A short story, a postcard or a description is 'sammenhængende tekster ... i en kendt teksttype' and 'udtrykke sig i skrift ... og billede'.

2:digraphs.why: Only if rebuilt for Danish (ng, sj, hv, nd, ld; there is no sh): finding the letter team while reading sentences is reading 'almindelige ikke-lydrette ord'.

2:sentence-boundaries.why: Stort begyndelsesbogstav and punktum or spørgsmålstegn are part of expressing oneself 'i skrift'; they are needed for a 'sammenhængende tekst'.

2:cursive-writing.why: Joined handwriting is a tool for 'udtrykke sig i skrift'; the binding text does not name håndskrift, and many Danish schools teach it in 2.-3. klasse or only lightly.

2:cloze-context.why: Using the story to choose the missing word is reading 'enkle tekster' with understanding.

2:question-words.why: Finding the question that fits a marked answer needs reading with understanding; forming questions prepares communication.

2:read-and-answer.why: Reading a short story and answering from the text is to 'læse enkle tekster sikkert'; 'Fortolkning' asks for conversation, which a sheet only prepares.

2:describe-a-picture.why: Sentences about a picture are a description: 'sammenhængende tekster på mindst 3 linjer i en kendt teksttype'.

2:word-classes.why: Sorting into navneord, udsagnsord and tillægsord gives 'opmærksomhed på sprog'; the goal is about communicating and no goal names ordklasser.

2:plural-nouns.why: Writing flertal (-er, -e, -r and irregular: mand - mænd, barn - børn) is spelling common, partly 'ikke-lydrette' word forms.

2:spelling-rules.why: The English rules named do not exist in Danish; rebuilt with Danish rules (dobbeltkonsonant after a short vowel, stumt d in nd/ld, stumt h in hv/hj) it is spelling 'almindelige ikke-lydrette ord'.

2:synonyms.why: Synonyms, and other words for 'sagde', are vocabulary for reading and for one's own writing; no goal names it.

2:synonyms~doing-stage.why: Synonyms, and other words for 'sagde', are vocabulary for reading and for one's own writing; no goal names it.

2:verb-forms.why: Nutid and datid (er - var, har - havde, gør - gjorde, går - gik) is attention to language; these forms are among the 'almindelige ikke-lydrette ord' (the point's own example is 'siger').

2:pronouns.why: Linking a pronoun to its name helps the reading of connected text and is attention to language; no goal names stedord.

2:read-cursive.why: Reading joined handwriting is not named anywhere; it serves reading simple everyday texts written by hand.

2:compound-words.why: Sammensatte ord, written as one word and sometimes with a joining s or e, are a central part of Danish spelling of common words.

2:root-words.why: Finding the shared root supports reading and spelling 'ikke-lydrette' words; the points do not name morphemes.

2:prefixes.why: Forstavelser (u-, mis-, gen-, for-) are attention to how words are built; in Denmark usually 3.-4. klasse work, and no goal names it.

2:retell-with-starters.why: A retelling in order with 'Først, Så, Derefter, Til sidst' is a 'sammenhængende tekst ... i en kendt teksttype'.

2:mystery-animal.why: Reading clues one at a time and using them is to 'læse enkle tekster ... og bruge dem'; the animal knowledge touches natur/teknologi.

2:animal-fact-file.why: Writing facts about an animal is expressing oneself 'i skrift' about a well-known subject and knowledge of nature; a fact file prepares writing 'i velkendte faglige situationer'.

2:compare-two-animals.why: Comparing facts about two animals is knowledge of nature read from simple fact sentences.

3:cursive-sentences.why: Joined handwriting is a tool for 'udtrykke sig i skrift'; the binding text does not name håndskrift.

3:word-fields.why: Telling close verbs apart (gå - slentre - styrte) is vocabulary for precise writing and for reading; no goal names it.

3:person-words.why: Forming bage - bager, løbe - løber is word building: it supports reading new words and goes beyond the spelling of common words in the point efter 2. klassetrin.

3:root-words-in-context.why: Choosing bage / bager / bagning / bagte for a sentence is word-form knowledge for writing; it goes beyond the spelling point efter 2. klassetrin.

K:human-body.why: Naming body parts comes before choices 'der styrker og udvikler kroppen' and before labelling a lifelike model of the body in natur/teknologi; BH.0.K3 speaks only of moving observantly in nature.

K:living-nonliving.why: Telling living from non-living is the 'viden' a child needs to 'færdes iagttagende i naturen'.

K:fruit-vegetable.why: Which part of the plant we eat is knowledge about plants for observing nature; it prepares 'genkende natur ... i sin hverdag'.

K:animal-groups-homes.why: Knowing animals and where they live is the 'viden' for 'færdes iagttagende i naturen'.

K:animal-babies.why: Animal young and their parents is knowledge about animals for observing nature.

K:seasons.why: Årstiderne and a tree through the year is exactly observing nature 'ud fra viden og erfaring'.

K:day-night.why: Day sky and night sky is a 'naturfagligt fænomen' the child observes.

K:weather-temperature.why: Observing the weather over a week is 'færdes iagttagende i naturen'.

K:natural-made.why: Natural or made by people is the very distinction of 'genkende natur og teknologi i sin hverdag', one year early.

K:five-senses.why: The senses are how a child is 'iagttagende'; knowing them belongs to the 'naturfaglige fænomener' area.

K:recycling.why: Sorting waste is technology and nature in everyday life ('genkende natur og teknologi i sin hverdag'); the børnehaveklasse goal speaks only of nature.

K:plant-needs.why: What a plant needs is knowledge for observing nature; it prepares simple investigations (growing cress).

K:sink-float.why: Floating and sinking is a 'naturfagligt fænomen' met through experience; it prepares 'enkle undersøgelser'.

1:animal-classes-coverings.why: Grouping animals by fur, feathers, scales or skin is recognising nature in an ordered way ('genkende natur ... i sin hverdag').

1:habitats-needs.why: Where animals live and what they need is knowledge of nature around the child.

1:life-cycles.why: A drawn life cycle of chicken, butterfly, frog or plant is a 'naturtro model' the child uses to say what comes next.

1:sink-float.why: Predict and test is 'udføre enkle undersøgelser' when the test is really done with objects; writing down what happened prepares 'beskrive egne undersøgelser'.

1:body-parts.why: Labelling a figure of the body is using a 'naturtro model'; the body words are needed for the talk about 'krop' in SSF.

1:five-senses.why: Which sense for which thing is knowledge about one's own body in everyday life; the senses are the tools of 'enkle undersøgelser'.

1:weather.why: Weather symbols and a weekly forecast are nature and technology met in everyday life.

1:materials-recycling.why: What things are made of and what is recycled is 'genkende natur og teknologi i sin hverdag'.

1:plant-parts.why: A labelled plant drawing is a 'naturtro model'; root, stem, leaf and flower are met in everyday nature.

1:sun-earth-moon.why: Pictures of sun, earth and the moon's phases are lifelike models; the moon is nature the child sees. In Denmark the solar system is more often 3.-4. klasse.

2:materials.why: Grouping things by material for recycling is 'genkende natur og teknologi i sin hverdag'.

2:plant-parts.why: The labelled plant is a 'naturtro model'; which part we eat ties it to everyday life.

2:life-cycles.why: Ordering the butterfly's life cycle uses a lifelike model of something seen in nature.

2:moon-phases.why: Pictures of the moon's phases are a lifelike model of what the child can see in the sky.

2:day-and-night.why: The turning Earth and the Sun (globe and lamp) is a lifelike model; explaining a cause with it leads to 'modeller med stigende abstraktionsgrad'.

2:habitats-adaptations.why: Who lives in a habitat is recognising nature; linking a body feature to the place prepares 'relatere natur ... til andre kontekster'.

2:sink-float.why: Predicting, testing and changing the shape of the clay is 'udføre enkle undersøgelser' when really done; the record prepares 'beskrive egne undersøgelser'.

3:water-cycle.why: Vandets kredsløb is a model that shows what cannot be seen at once: 'modeller med stigende abstraktionsgrad'.

3:flower-parts.why: A flower diagram with the job of each part is using a model beyond the plain lifelike picture.

3:life-cycles-compare.why: Comparing two life-cycle diagrams is using models at a more abstract level.

3:planets.why: The order of the planets is read from a model of the solar system: 'modeller med stigende abstraktionsgrad'.

3:investigation.why: Predict, test, record and conclude is 'gennemføre enkle undersøgelser på baggrund af egne forventninger', when the sheet is the record of a real test.

K:birds-eye-view.why: Matching a side view to the view from above is spatial readiness for geometry and for using a map as a model; no børnehaveklasse wording covers it.

K:family.why: Family words are vocabulary work in the 'Sprog' area; a family tree prepares history's link to 'eget liv' over time.

K:transport-flying.why: Vehicles on land, water and in the air are technology in everyday life ('genkende ... teknologi i sin hverdag'); the børnehaveklasse goals do not name technology.

K:wants-needs.none: No subject of these years holds economics or civics (samfundsfag starts in 8. klasse).
K:wants-needs.why: Nothing in the listed wording speaks of wants and needs.

K:community-helpers.none: No goal of these years names jobs or community helpers (samfundsfag starts in 8. klasse).
K:community-helpers.why: BH.0.K6 is about the child's own contribution to the group, not about knowing professions.

1:map-key.why: A simple picture map with a key is a model of a place the child reads: 'anvende naturtro modeller'. The binding text no longer names maps.

1:family-generations.why: Generations and one's own family tree are the first step toward relating change 'over tid til eget liv'; history itself starts in 3. klasse.

2:cardinal-directions.why: Using nord, syd, øst and vest on a simple map is using a model; the map with directions leads to more abstract models.

2:continents.why: A world map is a more abstract model than the 'naturtro modeller' efter 2. klassetrin; verdensdelene are usually 3.-4. klasse in Denmark.

2:family-relationships.why: Kinship words (moster / faster, fætter / kusine, mormor / farmor) prepare talking about family over time; no goal names them.

3:continents-oceans.why: Locating continents and oceans on a world map is using a model 'med stigende abstraktionsgrad'.

K:healthy-food.why: Everyday foods and sometimes foods are about 'valg, der styrker og udvikler kroppen'.

K:hygiene-habits.why: Hand washing and body care is to 'drage omsorg for sig selv' and a choice that keeps the body well.

K:road-safety.why: Reading the signal and crossing in the right steps is the start of 'færdes sikkert i trafikken'; the list places the goal in years 1-3, so the K sheets prepare it.

1:food-groups.why: Sorting foods into groups is knowledge behind 'hvad der fremmer sundhed'; the sheet sorts and does not yet explain. Danish schools use De officielle Kostråd, not four food groups.

1:healthy-habits.why: Tooth brushing, stopping germs and a habit chart of one's own week are 'hvad der fremmer sundhed og trivsel i eget liv'.

1:road-signs.why: Knowing what traffic signs mean is needed to 'færdes sikkert i trafikken i lokalområdet'.

2:healthy-habits-why.why: Saying what each habit protects is to 'forklare, hvad der fremmer sundhed'.

2:road-signs.why: Kinds of signs (advarselstavler, forbudstavler, oplysningstavler) and which fits a situation is knowledge for 'færdes sikkert i trafikken'.

K:how-to-draw.why: Drawing a picture is to 'udtrykke sig i billeder'; step-by-step drawing is technique more than free expression.

1:how-to-draw.why: Drawing a figure and placing it in a scene is making 'plane ... billeder'; copying steps is technique, the scene is the expression.

2:drawing.why: Drawing and then writing about it is 'udtrykke sig i plane ... billeder' and 'i skrift ... og billede'.

K:same-different-visual.none: Visual discrimination of pictures is not a goal of børnehaveklassen.
K:same-different-visual.why: It is readiness for seeing letter and number forms, but no wording names it.

K:mazes.why: Only the number routes ('ordne talsymbolerne') and the letter and beginning-sound routes ('bogstavernes form ... og lyd') fit; the plain mazes have no goal.

K:shadow-closure.none: Shadow matching and visual closure are perception puzzles with no goal.
K:shadow-closure.why: No wording of børnehaveklassen names visual perception.

K:spot-the-difference.none: Spot-the-difference is a perception puzzle with no goal.
K:spot-the-difference.why: No wording of børnehaveklassen names visual comparison of pictures.

K:matrix-logic.none: A picture-logic grid is a thinking puzzle with no goal.
K:matrix-logic.why: It uses neither number nor geometric language, so BH.0.K2 does not fit.

K:grid-copy.why: Copying square by square trains position in a grid, a step before 'anvende geometriske begreber'; no børnehaveklasse wording covers it.

1:find-the-differences.none: Finding differences between two pictures is a perception puzzle with no goal.
1:find-the-differences.why: Neither Danish nor mathematics names visual discrimination.

1:mazes.none: Picture mazes are puzzles with no goal.
1:mazes.why: Finding a way through a maze is not 'en situation med matematik' in the sense of MAT.3.K1.

1:grid-copy.why: Copying a picture on squared paper by rows and columns prepares work with position and figures under 'geometriske begreber'.

1:picture-analogies.none: Picture analogies are a reasoning puzzle with no goal.
1:picture-analogies.why: No wording in Danish or mathematics names analogies.

1:secret-code.none: Decoding with a key is a puzzle with no goal.
1:secret-code.why: It is neither reading of words in the sense of DAN.2.O1 nor calculation.

1:picture-sudoku.none: Picture sudoku is a logic puzzle with no goal.
1:picture-sudoku.why: It has no numbers or geometric content, so MAT.3.K1 does not really fit.

1:logic-picture-clues.none: A logic grid with picture clues is a puzzle with no goal.
1:logic-picture-clues.why: Deduction from clues is not named by any wording.

2:find-differences.why: Only the writing part fits: a sentence about each difference is to 'udtrykke sig i skrift'; the search itself has no goal.

2:logic-grid.none: A logic grid is a deduction puzzle with no goal.
2:logic-grid.why: The clues are read, but the skill is deduction, which no wording names.

3:two-attribute-sort.why: Sorting by two properties in a table or a Venn diagram is ordering data, part of 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

3:two-attribute-sort~logic-cabinet.why: Sorting by two properties in a table or a Venn diagram is ordering data, part of 'enkle statistiske undersøgelser'.

3:logic-grids.none: A logic grid is a deduction puzzle with no goal.
3:logic-grids.why: Deduction from clues is not named by any wording.

3:latin-square-sudoku.none: A 6x6 picture sudoku is a logic puzzle with no goal.
3:latin-square-sudoku.why: It has no number or geometric content, so MAT.3.K1 does not really fit.

K:feelings.why: Recognising and naming feelings is needed to 'drage omsorg for sig selv og andre'; it prepares 'trivsel i eget liv'.

K:measurable-attributes.none: not yet read against this curriculum
K:measurable-attributes.why: The point was added on 2026-11-13 for a lesson of the US school year that the teacher leads without a page; no unit of this language teaches it. Read it against the wording before a lesson of this language stands on it.

2:estimate-lengths.none: not yet read against this curriculum
2:estimate-lengths.why: The point was added on 2026-11-13 for a lesson of the US school year that the teacher leads without a page; no unit of this language teaches it. Read it against the wording before a lesson of this language stands on it.

2:explain-strategies.none: not yet read against this curriculum
2:explain-strategies.why: The point was added on 2026-11-13 for a lesson of the US school year that the teacher leads without a page; no unit of this language teaches it. Read it against the wording before a lesson of this language stands on it.

K:read-picture-book.none: not yet read against this curriculum
K:read-picture-book.why: The point was added on 2026-11-13 for the English mini-books (Part 8); a language gets its own books, and no unit of this language teaches the point yet. Read it against the wording when the first books of this language are written.

K:read-decodable-text.none: not yet read against this curriculum
K:read-decodable-text.why: The point was added on 2026-11-13 for the English mini-books (Part 8); a language gets its own books, and no unit of this language teaches the point yet. Read it against the wording when the first books of this language are written.

2:chance-certain-possible.why: Saying whether drawing a piece is certain, possible or impossible, and guessing what comes most often, is a first way to «udtrykke intuitive chancestørrelser»; the record sheet with tally and bars is an «enkel statistisk undersøgelse».

3:chance-more-likely.why: Deciding from which of two bags a piece is more likely is to «udtrykke intuitive chancestørrelser».
